question: The boundary line separating one drainage basin from another is called _________.
solution:
The correct answer is **__Watershed__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **watershed **is also commonly referred to as a **drainage basin**.
 
• A** watershed or drainage basin** is an area of land where all the water that falls within it, whether through rainfall or other sources, drains into a common outlet such as a river, lake, or ocean.
 
• It is a** natural topographic boundary that defines the area from which water flows downhill and converges into a single point**.
 
• The term "**drain**" refers to a **channel or pipe** used to **remove excess water, while a pond is a small body of water typically formed by damming or artificially creating a depression**.
 
• Although** a river is often part of a watershed**, a watershed refers to the entire land area that contributes to the flow of water into that river, including the surrounding hills, valleys, and tributaries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Types of Watersheds: They are classified depending on the size, drainage, shape, and land use pattern.

 
 
• Macro watershed (> 50,000 Ha)
 
• Sub-watershed (10,000 to 50,000 Ha)
 
• Milli-watershed (1000 to 10,000 Ha)
 
• Micro watershed (100 to 1000 Ha)
 
• Mini watershed (1-100 Ha)
 
 
 
• **Peneplain**
 
 
• It is the end product of the fluvial cycle of erosion in the Davisian cycle of erosion.
 
• At the end of the third stage, the relief is almost destroyed and the land surface appears as a flat featureless plain known as ‘peneplain’.
 
• The peneplain may have in its fold a few hills which have still not lost their existence despite wasting.
 
• Davis called these isolated hills as ‘Monadnocks’
 
 
 
• Floodplain
 
 
• Floodplains are generally **flat areas of land that lie next to a river or stream**, extending from the river banks to the outer edges of the valley.
 
• They comprise two parts: the main channel of the river, called a **floodway**; and the **flood fringe**, which is the area that floods occasionally.
 
• **Floodways **can sometimes be seasonal, meaning the channel is dry for part of the year.
 
• **Floodplains **are susceptible to flooding because of their low-lying topography near rivers.
